title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow?

items.stem: Which statement best separates a workflow from an agent?

options.text: A workflow uses tools to act, while an agent only writes text
A workflow calls the model one time, while an agent calls it more
In a workflow the code fixes the steps, while in an agent the model picks them
A workflow runs without any model, while an agent always has a model

items.stem: For every student message, a makerspace assistant does this. Step 1: one model call labels the message 'manual question' or 'booking request'. Step 2: if the label is 'manual question', the code searches the manuals and makes a second model call to write the answer; if it is 'booking request', the code runs a fixed booking routine. Who owns the control flow, and what is this system?

options.text: The model owns it, so this is an agent, because its label picks the branch
The code owns it, so this is a workflow, because the code defines every branch
The model owns it, so this is an agent, because it calls the model twice
The code owns it, so this is a workflow, because it never uses any tool

items.stem: Which of these makerspace tasks is the worst fit for a fixed workflow, because its steps cannot be written down in advance?

options.text: Telling a student the laser cutter's opening hours from one manual page
Booking a slot once the student has confirmed the time they asked for
Sending a reminder the day before each booking, always in the same form
Finding why a student's print failed, where each next check depends on the last result

items.stem: A fixed workflow for booking always makes 2 model calls per request. An agent doing the same job averages 6 model calls per request. Assume every model call costs $0.004 and nothing else costs money. How many dollars does the workflow save over 500 requests?

A program takes a student's question and makes one model call to draft an answer. Its code then always makes a second model call to check the draft against the manual, and then returns the result. Answer with one word: is this a workflow or an agent?

At the design review, a teammate says: 'Booking should be an agent, because agents are more advanced.' Booking always means checking the calendar, then writing the booking, then confirming it. Which reply best defends a fixed workflow?

options.text: The steps are known in advance, so code can run them with fewer model calls and fewer surprises
Agents are more accurate on every task, but the sponsor's budget is too small to pay for that
A workflow is the better choice only when the model is too weak to decide the next step
An agent cannot call a calendar tool, because only code that is fixed in advance can call tools
